action_items.task: Prepare for the next meeting to discuss detailed design.
Write up product evaluation plan and details on physical makeup.
Inquire about where to obtain clay for prototyping.

decisions.text: Conventional batteries will be used instead of solar or kinetic cells.
Rubber material will be used for the casing.
The remote will have a double-curved design to accommodate ergonomic needs for left and right-handed users.
The interface will include a joystick, two function buttons, and an LCD, excluding a numeric keypad.
Agreed to use a spongy rubber texture for the remote control.
Selected bright yellow as the primary color for the remote control.
Decided to include on-board memory for the remote control.
Agreed to support international use with different languages and skins.

notes:
## Design Overview and Materials
- The design is based on minimal requirements from the previous meeting including a joystick, LCD, navigation buttons, and a power button.
- Marketing research indicates users prioritize aesthetics and perceived capability over functionality, preferring a 'cool' look.
- The case material is rubber for an ergonomic feel suitable for both left and right-handed users, rejecting plastic, titanium, and wood.
- The shape is double-curved to accommodate ergonomic needs, though it limits material options compared to single-curved designs.
- The design is articulated at two points to allow adjustment for handedness.
## Interface and Features
- The interface includes a joystick, two function buttons, and an LCD display; a numeric keypad was dropped.
- Basic mode uses the joystick for channel and volume control, while menu mode is accessed via buttons.
- The top button serves as On/Off in basic mode and Enter in menu mode; bottom buttons switch modes.
- Programming is primarily done via a computer cable for ease, but a non-computer programming mode is retained for compatibility.
- The device requires on-board memory to store menu settings and user customizations.
- USB connectivity is discussed for PC programming, though cost concerns were noted.
- The device will support international use with different languages and skins.
## Power and Components
- Conventional batteries are selected instead of solar or kinetic energy sources.
- The Industrial Designer presented slides covering components, findings, and internal workings, including the chip's role in translating key presses to infrared signals.
- Buttons may include a scroll wheel (requires an expensive chip) or a number keypad; LCD requires a more powerful chip than standard button transmission.
## Aesthetics and Branding
- Consensus on a spongy rubber texture for the remote control.
- Preference for bright yellow color to make the device harder to lose.
- The design rejects the fruit and vegetable theme.
- The device will include the company slogan.
## Advanced Features
- Marketing proposes a universal remote that auto-finds TV frequencies, though the UI Designer notes this is technically complex due to different command sets per manufacturer.
- Project Manager suggests an LCD lookup feature where users enter the TV brand name to find codes, avoiding the need for a physical booklet.
- Marketing suggests a 'monkey noise' sound effect when the remote is lost to help locate it.
- Project Manager suggests a double curved design with a flexible rubber outer skin and a firm inner sub-structure to avoid structural weakness.
- Industrial Designer suggests a banana shape if using the fruit/veg theme.
tldr: The team finalized the conceptual design of a remote control with a spongy rubber texture, bright yellow color, and double-curved shape, settling on conventional batteries and an LCD interface while rejecting fruit/vegetable themes.
